addedLines: - claude: Catch-all for any task that doesn't fit a more specific agent. FleetView's default when no agent name is typed. (Tools: *)

- Explore: Fast read-only search agent for locating code. Use it to find files by pattern (eg. "src/components/**/*.tsx"), grep for symbols or keywords (eg. "API endpoints"), or answer "where is X defined / which files reference Y." Do NOT use it for code review, design-doc auditing, cross-file consistency checks, or open-ended analysis — it reads excerpts rather than whole files and will miss content past its read window. When calling, specify search breadth: "quick" for a single targeted lookup, "medium" for moderate exploration, or "very thorough" to search across multiple locations and naming conventions. (Tools: All tools except Agent, Artifact, ExitPlanMode, Edit, Write, NotebookEdit)

- general-purpose: General-purpose agent for researching complex questions, searching for code, and executing multi-step tasks. When you are searching for a keyword or file and are not confident that you will find the right match in the first few tries use this agent to perform the search for you. (Tools: *)

- Plan: Software architect agent for designing implementation plans. Use this when you need to plan the implementation strategy for a task. Returns step-by-step plans, identifies critical files, and considers architectural trade-offs. (Tools: All tools except Agent, Artifact, ExitPlanMode, Edit, Write, NotebookEdit)
- statusline-setup: Use this agent to configure the user's Claude Code status line setting. (Tools: Read, Edit)

- dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo). Omit the interval to let the model self-pace. - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- claude-api: Reference for the Claude API / Anthropic SDK — model ids, pricing, params, streaming, tool use, MCP, agents, caching, token counting, model migration.
TRIGGER — read BEFORE opening the target file; don't skip because it "looks like a one-liner" — whenever: the prompt names Claude/Anthropic in any form (Claude, Anthropic, Fable, Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, `anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai`, `claude-*`, `us.anthropic.*`, `[1m]`); the user asks about an LLM (pricing/model choice/limits/caching) — never answer from memory; OR the task is LLM-shaped with provider unstated (agent/MCP/tool-definition/multi-agent/RAG/LLM-judge/computer-use; generate/summarize/extract/classify/rewrite/converse over NL; debugging refusals/cutoffs/streaming/tool-calls/tokens).
SKIP only when another provider is being worked on (overrides all triggers): OpenAI/GPT/Gemini/Llama/Mistral/Cohere/Ollama named in the query; OR `grep -rE 'openai|langchain_openai|google.generativeai|genai|mistralai|cohere|ollama'` over the project hits (run this grep FIRST if no provider named — don't Read the file).
- run: Launch and drive this project's app to see a change working. Use when asked to run, start, or screenshot the app, or to confirm a change works in the real app (not just tests). First looks for a project skill that already covers launching the app; otherwise falls back to built-in patterns per project type (CLI, server, TUI, Electron, browser-driven, library).
- init: Initialize a new CLAUDE.md file with codebase documentation
- review: Review a GitHub pull request; for your working diff use /code-review
- security-review: Complete a security review of the pending changes on the current branch

136	  /// history via `selectedTargetID.didSet` — used by *deliberate* actions (drop, remove-reselect). The
137	  /// incidental click-to-focus path (a surface becoming first responder) routes through a
138	  /// history-suppressed setter instead (see the focus callback), so co-monitoring glances don't spam ⌘[.
139	  func focusWorkroomMember(_ sid: SidebarID) {

144	  /// Insert `sid` beside `beside` on `edge`. Joins `beside`'s existing group, or seeds a **new** group
145	  /// from the two of them (leaving any other group untouched — a window holds many groups);
146	  /// **removes `sid` from its current group first** so dragging an existing pane to a new edge is a
147	  /// *move*, not a duplicate. Focuses the inserted member. No-op for a self-drop or non-resolving leaf.
148	  /// Mirrors `TerminalSessions.moveTabIntoSplit`.
149	  func insertWorkroomSplit(_ sid: SidebarID, beside: SidebarID, edge: PaneEdge) {
150	    // Reject a self-drop, a non-resolving leaf (`.project` / deleted workroom), and a workroom whose
151	    // directory is gone (`isMissing`) — a missing leaf would render a "Directory not found" pane that
152	    // can only be backed out of again, so don't let one into the split in the first place (#23).
153	    guard sid != beside, let dropped = target(for: sid), !dropped.isMissing,
154	      target(for: beside) != nil
155	    else { return }
156	    // Leave whatever group `sid` was in (possibly dissolving it) BEFORE joining `beside`'s — structural
157	    // only, no selection re-point: `sid` is about to be focused anyway.
158	    detachFromSplitGroup(sid)
159	    if let index = splitIndex(containing: beside) {
160	      workroomSplits[index] = workroomSplits[index].inserting(
161	        sid, beside: beside, orientation: edge.orientation,
162	        newLeafFirst: edge.placesDroppedFirst, ratio: 0.5)
163	    } else {
164	      let dropped = PaneLayout<SidebarID>.leaf(sid)
165	      let anchor = PaneLayout<SidebarID>.leaf(beside)
166	      workroomSplits.append(
167	        .split(
168	          id: UUID(), orientation: edge.orientation, ratio: 0.5,
169	          first: edge.placesDroppedFirst ? dropped : anchor,
170	          second: edge.placesDroppedFirst ? anchor : dropped))
171	    }
172	    focusWorkroomMember(sid)
173	  }
174	
175	  /// Structural-only removal of `sid` from its group: collapse to the survivor subtree, or drop the
176	  /// group entirely when fewer than two members remain. Deliberately does NOT touch the selection —
177	  /// used by the move path, which focuses the moved member itself. No-op when `sid` isn't grouped.
178	  private func detachFromSplitGroup(_ sid: SidebarID) {
179	    guard let index = splitIndex(containing: sid) else { return }

166	    // is a *sibling* above it, never a wrapper around it. A structural
167	    // `if multi { VStack { titleBar; content } } else { content }` would swap SwiftUI's
168	    // `_ConditionalContent` branch when a 2-member split dissolves to solo, tearing down + rebuilding

170	    // This mirrors `PaneLeafView`, which keeps its content in one slot and expresses the `multiPane`
171	    // chrome as always-mounted overlays (issue #3).
172	    //
173	    // Since issue #139 the title bar is UNCONDITIONAL, which strengthens that invariant rather than
174	    // straining it: with no `if` there is no branch left to flip on this axis. The hazard of the same
175	    // shape that remains is the missing-directory choice, which is why `TargetTerminalDetail` owns it
176	    // as a ZStack sibling rather than this view branching on it.
177	    VStack(spacing: 0) {
178	      // Every workroom is identified by its own header (issue #139), which in a split also names
179	      // *which* member this is and offers the way back out of the group.
180	      WorkroomPaneTitleBar(
181	        target: target, projectPath: projectPath, projectLabel: projectLabel,
182	        workroomName: workroomName, focused: focused,
183	        controls: toolbarControls, onClose: onClose
184	      )
185	      // Drag the group by its title bar to move the whole member within the split (issue #110) —
186	      // the SAME gesture/closures the tab-bar chip uses, so it drops onto the same panes and shows
187	      // the same drop-edge highlight. A plain click (no movement past `minimumDistance`) still
188	      // falls through to the leaf's focus tap.
189	      //
190	      // `including:` MUST be `.subviews` (not `.none`) when solo: `GestureMask.none` disables every
191	      // gesture in the SUBVIEW hierarchy as well as the added one, which would kill this bar's own
192	      // Run / Open-in buttons in exactly the single-workroom case issue #139 exists to serve — and
193	      // `ToolbarIconButtonStyle`'s hover well is `.onHover`, not a gesture, so they would still light
194	      // up and look alive. `.subviews` drops only the drag.
195	      .gesture(
196	        DragGesture(minimumDistance: 6, coordinateSpace: .global)
197	          .onChanged { value in
198	            externalDrag = localize(value.location).map {
199	              WorkroomPaneDrag(sid: sid, location: $0)
200	            }
201	          }
202	          .onEnded { value in
203	            if let drop = dropTarget(value.location), drop.sid != sid {

303	///
304	/// It takes the "is there anything to show" facts as inputs rather than letting each control decide for
305	/// itself, because the group divider depends on **both** its neighbours: a separator with nothing on one
306	/// side of it is worse than no separator. Deriving every flag here, in one pass, is what makes it
307	/// impossible for the divider to disagree with the buttons it separates.
308	enum WorkroomPaneToolbarPresentation {
309	  struct Controls: Equatable {
310	    let run: Bool
311	    let openIn: Bool
312	    /// The rule between the run group and "Open in…" — only when both are actually there.
313	    let divider: Bool
314	    let removeFromSplit: Bool
315	  }
316	
317	  static func controls(
318	    isMissing: Bool, projectPath: String?, hasEditor: Bool, multi: Bool
319	  ) -> Controls {
320	    // Run is deliberately NOT gated on a configured command: the button is always there for a present
321	    // target, and pressing it with nothing configured opens Project Settings with the warning, the same
322	    // as ⌘R (issue #139 follow-up). It still needs an owning project, since that's what a command would
323	    // be keyed to. "Open in…" is gated, because with no editor installed there is nowhere to open.
324	    let run = !isMissing && projectPath != nil
325	    let openIn = !isMissing && hasEditor

332	/// a leading identity glyph, the `project / workroom` label (matching the tab chip's format), and a
333	/// trailing toolbar carrying this workroom's own actions — "Open in…", run/stop/restart, and (for a
334	/// real split member) the remove-from-split ✕. It spans the pane's full width and, together with the
335	/// leaf's rounded card, makes each pane read as a distinct, identifiable unit. Reflects focus by colour
336	/// (accent + full-strength text when focused, muted otherwise), the pane's selection signal.
337	///

339	/// co-displayed split member's were unreachable; here each pane owns its own and acts on its own
340	/// target.

343	  let projectPath: String?
344	  /// The project name, derived (with `workroomName`) by the leaf — which needs it for the close prompt

348	  let focused: Bool
349	  /// Resolved by the leaf, which has the store — this view stays store-free on purpose (see

351	  let controls: WorkroomPaneToolbarPresentation.Controls
352	  let onClose: () -> Void
353	  @Environment(\.accessibilityReduceMotion) private var reduceMotion
354	  private let theme = ThemeService.shared
355	
356	  var body: some View {
357	    HStack(spacing: 6) {
358	      // Leading glyph mirrors the tab chip's: a house for a project root, a cube for a workroom
359	      // (`workroomName` is nil only for a root). Accent on the focused pane, muted otherwise.
360	      Image(systemName: workroomName == nil ? "house" : "cube")
361	        .font(.system(size: 10))
362	        .foregroundStyle(focused ? theme.tokens.accent : theme.tokens.fgMuted)
363	      if target.isMissing {
364	        Image(systemName: "exclamationmark.triangle.fill")
365	          .font(.system(size: 10))
366	          .foregroundStyle(.orange)
367	          .help("Directory not found")
368	      }
369	      // `project / workroom`, same format and size as `WorkroomTabChip`. Full-strength on the focused
370	      // member, muted otherwise — the brighter header is the in-content "this is the active pane" cue.
371	      HStack(alignment: .firstTextBaseline, spacing: 4) {
372	        Text(projectLabel)
373	          .foregroundStyle(focused ? Color.primary : theme.tokens.fgMuted)
374	        if let workroomName {
375	          Text("/").foregroundStyle(.tertiary)
376	          Text(workroomName)
377	            .foregroundStyle(focused ? Color.primary : theme.tokens.fgMuted)
378	        }
379	      }

content.text:
Based on my analysis of the diff and reading of the changed files:

**Change summary:** This is a pure UI/refactoring change with no security-relevant surface area:
1. `AppStore.swift` — Two assignments (`selectedTargetID`, `selectedProjectID`) delegated to existing `focusWorkroomMember(sid)` which does the exact same two assignments. Semantically identical.
2. `TabReorderMath.swift` — Adds a shared `TabStripMetrics.maxChipTitle: CGFloat = 180` constant (pure layout number).
3. `TerminalTabStrip.swift`, `WorkroomTabBar.swift` — Replace three duplicated `180` layout constants with the shared one.
4. `WorkroomSplitView.swift` — Passes an already-derived `projectLabel` (from `NSString.lastPathComponent` of an in-app project path used only for display) into a child view instead of recomputing it there; refactors `WorkroomSplitDivider`'s drag gesture into a shared `dragged(from:by:)` helper that computes the same clamped ratio, drops a redundant `latest` `@State`.
5. `UITestFixture.swift`, `TabStripOverflowUITests.swift` — Comment/reference updates only.

**Sinks touched:** none. No shell/exec, filesystem writes, network calls, deserialization, SQL, logging of sensitive values, auth/permission checks, IPC handlers, or serialization sinks are added or modified. The `projectLabel` derivation is a display-only `lastPathComponent` on a path already in-app; the drag math still passes through the pre-existing `PaneTreeLayout.clampRatio` invariant.

**Behavioral equivalence checks:**
- `focusWorkroomMember(sid)` (line 139 of `AppStore+WorkroomSplit.swift`) performs the identical two assignments the diff removed.
- New `dragged(from:by:)` reproduces the prior inline formula (`start + delta / max(1, total - dividerThickness)` then `clampRatio`) verbatim; the `.onEnded` guard on `startRatio` correctly makes a no-move gesture commit nothing (a hardening improvement over the prior `latest`-based path).

No source→sink taint paths, no authorization/parsing/validation regressions, no observability/PII leaks, no fail-open state drift.
